The Crown Road. TWO VOICES AND NEITHER OF THEM IS ABOUT THE STORM, which is the point: this is the last quiet map in Act 5 and the last one before the eighth Hall, and after four maps of people saying the weather is wrong it would be a relief and a lie to have two more. So one of them is about a boundary stone nobody can reach and one is about a wall somebody cut nine hundred years ago, and both of them are quietly about the same thing the whole game is about -- what people leave behind them, and what the people who come after make of it.

The mason is the closest this road comes to Crownspire's argument. He works stone for a living, he has spent his life looking at something better than anything he can do, and he is not bitter about it.

lines: Out there on the islet. One stone, two faces, two names cut on it.
Skyreach on one side and Crownspire on the other, and eight hundred years of arguing.
Nobody has ever got out to it to see which way round they are. That is the joke.
I cut stone. Thirty years. That arch was cut by somebody who was better than me.
No mortar in it. None. It has stood through everything and it holds itself up.
I come and look at it when a job has gone badly. It has never once cheered me up.
Granite, and the same granite the city wall is, and older than the city wall.
It is a doorway with no building. It was here before the road that goes through it.
